speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, could you tell me exactly which antibiotic you were taking and for how long before these symptoms started? Also, can you describe what the rash looks like and where on your body it is most prominent?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
The complement levels are normal, which makes serum sickness less likely given the typical hypocomplementemia. Has the patient experienced any swelling of the face or lips, and are the joint pains accompanied by visible swelling or just tenderness?

REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgE_Level

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal IgE level makes an immediate allergic reaction unlikely. Has the patient had any recent sore throat or skin infection prior to the sinusitis, and are the joint pains accompanied by visible swelling or just tenderness?

REQUEST TEST: ASO_Titer

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal ASO titer makes post-streptococcal reactive arthritis unlikely. Since the symptoms started a week after starting amoxicillin and involve fever, rash, and joint pain, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of Serum Sickness-Like Reaction (SSLR), which often presents with normal complement levels.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum Sickness-Like Reaction
